title: Senior Partner Deployed Engineer
description: The Role We are looking for a Senior Partner Deployed Engineer to join the Customer Solutions team, focused on building Coder’s partner ecosystem across EMEA. This is a new function at Coder, modeled on the Forward Deployed Engineer role pioneered by companies like Palantir and now the fastest-growing technical role at frontier AI companies. The difference: instead of embedding with a single customer to deploy a platform, you embed with strategic partners to help them understand, position, and deliver Coder’s platform across their entire customer base. You are part Field CTO, part Industry Strategist, part Technical Specialist, and part Partner Relations Lead. You will be the technical authority within our EMEA partner ecosystem: setting the vision for how Coder fits into each partner’s AI, cloud, and modernization offerings, co-creating the GTM sales plays that partner sellers take to market, building the demonstrations and workshops that generate pipeline, and producing the Partner Relations content that establishes Coder’s technical brand in the ecosystem. This is not a support role. You are equally comfortable holding a strategic roadmap conversation with a partner CTO and debugging a Kubernetes deployment in a partner’s lab in the same afternoon. You are energized by the challenge of building a new category through partnerships, motivated by the multiplied impact of enabling an entire ecosystem rather than a single customer, and capable of operating with full autonomy in a fast-moving startup environment. What You’ll Do Serve as the strategic technical thought partner to EMEA partner leadership, including practice leads, CTOs, and solutions architects at global systems integrators, regional cloud consultancies, and hyperscaler field teams. Own the technical relationship and set the vision for how Coder fits into each partner’s AI and modernization portfolio. Co-create sales plays tailored to each partner’s customer base, vertical focus, and services capabilities. Author Working Backwards outcome proposals for strategic partner-customer combinations that translate AI Development Infrastructure into deal-level urgency. Develop and deliver workshops, Builder Labs, and partner-hosted enablement sessions as the primary awareness and demand generation vehicle for the EMEA ecosystem. Build hands-on demonstration environments and interactive experiences that partners can use independently. Intervene directly on the highest-value partner-attached deals across EMEA: co-sell calls, technical discovery, PoV scoping, architecture review, and technical win support. Own the engagement until the partner’s team can carry it independently. Transform bespoke partner enablement sessions into structured LMS modules and certification tiers that scale across the EMEA partner base without requiring live PDE support for each new partner. Produce “better together” reference architectures for strategic partner combinations across cloud providers and AI platforms. Include deployment diagrams, network topology, IAM patterns, and operational runbooks that partner SAs can hand directly to customers. Codify each successful partner engagement into a repeatable GTM play: trigger conditions, discovery questions, positioning framework, demo script, PoV scope template, and expected outcomes. Build a playbook library that a new PDE or partner seller can pick up and run. Build AI-powered self-service tools that automate high-volume PDE activities: Opportunity Brief Generator, PR/FAQ Generator, Workshop-in-a-Box deployment, and demo site builder. Produce a monthly partner intelligence digest from EMEA engagements: what customers are asking for, how competitors are positioning, where integrations are missing, which vertical use cases are emerging. Distribute to Product, Engineering, and GTM leadership. Own the EMEA-relevant portions of the joint technical integration roadmap with strategic partners. Define priorities cross-functionally with Product and Engineering based on field signals from the EMEA market. Create and publish Partner Relations content, the ecosystem equivalent of Developer Relations: technical blog posts, cookbooks, partner ecosystem conference talks, enablement videos, and workshop recaps. Build Coder’s technical brand within the EMEA partner community. Contribute to cloud marketplace product listing stewardship, competency maintenance documentation, and CSP co-build technical requirements as they apply to EMEA-specific partner and compliance contexts. What We’re Looking For 7+ years of experience in a combination of Forward Deployed Engineering, Solutions Architecture, Field CTO, Technical Consulting, or Developer Relations roles at an infrastructure, developer tools, or AI company Demonstrated experience helping partners or customers understand and adopt products in emerging or undefined categories, not just executing playbooks for established ones Proven hands-on experience designing and deploying cloud infrastructure on at least one major cloud provider (AWS, Google Cloud, or Microsoft Azure), with production-level Kubernetes and Terraform depth. You have done the work and can speak to it with specificity. 2+ years deploying or operating AI coding agents in a production or near-production environment: you understand how agent loops execute, where credentials live, and what governance and audit requirements look like in a European enterprise context Ability to articulate the architectural difference between workspace-local agent tooling and a centralized agentic harness, and to explain why that distinction matters to a security, compliance, or data sovereignty stakeholder Experience working with channel or technology partners in a co-sell model: hyperscaler partner programs, GSI/RSI partnerships, or VAR/distributor ecosystems in EMEA markets Experience building repeatable technical GTM assets that scaled beyond your personal delivery: sales plays, enablement curricula, reference architectures, or technical content programs Executive communication and Field CTO credibility: you can hold a technical vision conversation with a partner CTO and a deal-level architecture review with an SE in the same day, in English and ideally at least one additional European language Strong written communication: you can produce a Working Backwards PR/FAQ, a technical architecture document, and a blog post without those being separate skills requiring separate people Self-directed, analytically minded, and comfortable operating with full autonomy. You will define processes that don’t exist, build tools that haven’t been scoped, and create a function from first principles in a new region. Bonus Points (Bonus tacos? That’s how we say thanks at Coder. Ask us about it.) Prior Forward Deployed Engineer experience at a platform company (Palantir, Scale AI, frontier AI lab, or equivalent embedded deployment model) Track record of public technical advocacy: blog posts, conference talks, open-source contributions, or developer/partner community engagement Experience with hyperscaler partner programs (e.g., ISV Accelerate, strategic collaboration agreements, co-sell programs) at an operational level Familiarity with European regulatory environments: GDPR, DORA, NIS2, AI Act compliance requirements, and data sovereignty patterns for cloud-native deployments Experience with air-gapped or network-isolated deployments common in European financial services, government, or defense contexts Background in AI governance frameworks, session audit requirements, or SIEM integration for AI workloads Experience with LLM gateway or proxy infrastructure (LiteLLM, OpenRouter, or equivalent) in a multi-team or enterprise context Experience designing human-in-the-loop breakpoints or escalation patterns for autonomous agent workflows Kubernetes certification (CKA, CKAD, or CKS) Experience with Tailscale or similar overlay networking tools Open-source contributions, particularly in CNCF, MCP, or AI agent ecosystems Existing relationships with hyperscaler EMEA solutions architecture teams, European GSI technical practices, or AI infrastructure partner ecosystems Fluency in German, French, or a Nordic language in addition to English What Success Looks Like You have done the hard technical work before: deploying cloud-native infrastructure, navigating Kubernetes in production, building with Terraform, and operating in the complexity of large European enterprise environments. You bring that credibility into every partner conversation. You can walk a partner CTO through how Coder enables parallelized AI agents in a regulated European enterprise, covering credential isolation, audit lineage, GDPR-compliant data handling, and escalation design, and turn that conversation into a joint GTM play their sellers can run next quarter. description: This role sits within the Onboarding & Incentives pillar of the Rider Growth function at Deliveroo, this pillar owns the journey from the moment an applicant expresses interest through to a fully habituated, retained rider. Senior Stakeholder Reporting : Ensure rider hours performance and initiative impact are reported accurately and clearly to senior stakeholders on a regular cadence. Weekly Applicant Target Setting : Own the weekly rider applicant target-setting process, ensuring targets reflect the latest view of demand, funnel performance, and onboarding capacity. Annual Planning : Lead applicant target setting within the annual planning cycle, working with Science and local Regional Operations teams to work back from onboard targets to applicant targets. Scenario Planning & Cost Efficiency : Run scenario planning with the Rider Marketing team to stress-test target and budget assumptions and identify opportunities to drive down cost per applicant. Cross-Functional Partnership : Build strong working relationships across Science, Regional Operations, Retention & Resurrection, and Rider Marketing to keep incentive, performance, and target-setting decisions aligned. description: About the team The Value Proposition & New Benefits team owns what our core value proposition for subscription should be, and the new benefits that bring it to life. About the role We're looking for a Strategy & Operations Manager to own strategy and execution for new benefits within Subscription. This is a hybrid strategy/build/run role: you'll define what to launch, then work cross-functionally to get it shipped and measure whether it's working. You'll be expected to move fluidly between strategic thinking and hands-on execution - this is not a role where strategy stops at a slide deck. Typical problems you'll solve: What new benefits should we launch for Subscription - which ideas are worth pursuing, and what's the business case for each? How do we prioritise and sequence a pipeline of benefit ideas against limited engineering, design, and operational capacity? How do we define success for a new benefit before launch - what does a good outcome look like, and what would tell us to kill it? Once live, how is a benefit actually performing - impact on acquisition, retention, frequency, and member satisfaction - against its cost to serve, and what does that tell us to do next? How do we take a benefit from a small pilot to a scaled, steady-state feature, and what needs to be true operationally for that to work? What you'll be doing Own the strategy and roadmap for new benefits within Subscription - build the analysis, the business case, and the plan, and drive it through to execution. Build and prioritise the benefit pipeline - evaluate a stream of ideas (experiential, use-case specific, or otherwise), size their potential impact and cost, and decide what's worth building next. Track ongoing performance - maintain visibility into each live benefit's impact on acquisition, retention, frequency, and satisfaction against its cost to serve, flagging when something needs attention. Scale what works - take benefits from small pilots to steady-state features, defining the operating model, reporting cadence, and processes needed to run them sustainably. Bring outside-in perspective - track what Uber One, DashPass, Wolt+, Just Eat and Amazon Prime are doing with membership benefits, and translate what's relevant into Deliveroo's context. Communicate to senior stakeholders - write clear strategy documents and present recommendations, trade-offs, and results to leadership. Requirements 5+ years of experience in strategy & operations, strategy consulting, or business operations - ideally with exposure to marketplaces, subscription/membership businesses, or consumer tech. Reporting to the CISO, you'll own the security roadmap for Pigment's product, infrastructure, and CI/CD environment, and you'll build much of it yourself. This is a hands-on role: expect to read code, threat model new services, reproduce and triage vulnerabilities, dig through infrastructure configuration and build the automation that closes gaps. You'll also set direction and bring product and engineering with you, but that influence comes from technical credibility and not process: the engineers you work with will take you seriously because you've been in the same code they have. The scope is broad: application security, infrastructure security, detection and response, and the assurance work that keeps our certifications standing. You won't be covering it alone. The security team is seven people and growing, with colleagues already owning compliance, governance and security operations, so this role can go deep on product and infrastructure and not be spread too thin across everything. Key responsibilities include: Product & Infrastructure Security Design - Design security features into the product itself and strengthen defence-in-depth across the platform. Threat model new services before they ship, and make the architectural calls that are expensive to reverse later. Security Review & Risk Assessment - Review code, architecture and configuration yourself, and be the person developers and PMs bring problems to early rather than late. Deliver solutions that balance risk against business benefit, and escalate the calls that genuinely need senior arbitration. Assurance & Testing - Run our assurance programme: internal code, architecture and configuration reviews, red team exercises, and the bug bounty. Own the relationship with third-party auditors, and measure the control KPIs that keep our certifications defensible. Vulnerability Management - Own vulnerabilities from detection through to verified fix: reproduce them, score and triage them, design or validate the mitigation, and confirm it actually worked. Improve the KPIs that tell you whether the process is holding. Detection Engineering - Build and improve our detection capability alongside the infrastructure and engineering teams: identify the signals worth collecting, write rules that catch real attacks without drowning us in noise, and build the response playbooks behind them. Incident Response - Lead security investigations into the production environment end to end, from first signal to root cause, across incidents and fraud. Flag the repetitive work worth automating and the detections worth building, and hand those to the security operations team. SDLC - Set the technical direction for how engineers at Pigment build securely: guidance, paved paths, and reviews that teach and not just gate. Contribute to company-wide awareness where it counts, but your primary audience is product, engineering and SRE.   Example projects that would fall under your responsibilities (actual examples of recently completed or currently on the roadmap): Secure the design and development of our AI features, including the MCP Server and Modeler Agent: threat modelling, design reviews, working alongside the engineers building them, and security assessments.  Work out where AI-assisted analysis actually belongs in our pipeline. title: Staff Security Engineer
description: Build security platforms, not security processes We are looking for a  Staff Security Engineer to strengthen the security of our products, data and engineering platform. This is a highly technical and hands-on role. You will work closely with Engineering teams to continuously harden our systems while helping design the next generation of our security architecture. You will operate across two horizons: Strengthen security today: continuously harden our applications, access controls and data-protection mechanisms against evolving threats. Build the privacy architecture of tomorrow: move beyond traditional perimeter and access-control security by designing systems where sensitive data is cryptographically isolated, minimally exposed, and increasingly usable without being directly revealed. The ultimate objective is not simply to make Swile harder to breach. It is to make a breach increasingly uninteresting, because there is less usable data available to steal. What you will do We want Security Engineering to create capabilities that scale across hundreds of engineers. You will: Identify and reduce high-impact security risks across our applications, APIs and internal tools. Strengthen authentication, authorization and access controls. Improve the protection of sensitive and personal data. Design controls that limit the blast radius of compromised accounts, services or infrastructure. Improve security monitoring, auditability and detection of suspicious access patterns. Perform threat modelling and targeted security reviews. Build reusable security capabilities directly into our engineering platform and development lifecycle. Contribute to long-term architectures around data isolation, encryption, tokenisation and privacy-preserving systems. Partner with engineering teams to address systemic security risks rather than individual findings. Where possible, a security requirement should become code rather than documentation. What we are looking for You are first and foremost a strong engineer. You have significant experience building or securing production software and distributed systems. You are comfortable reading and writing production code, designing systems and working directly with Engineering teams. You have deep security engineering expertise and strong experience in several of the following areas: Application and Product Security API Security IAM, authentication and authorization OAuth2 / OIDC, WebAuthn / FIDO2 RBAC / ABAC and privilege management Cloud security Cryptography, KMS / HSM and envelope encryption Tokenisation and secrets management Data Security and Privacy Engineering Threat modelling and secure software architecture Security monitoring and detection Stronger attacker mindset You naturally ask: What happens if this employee becomes malicious? What happens if this backend is compromised? What happens if someone dumps this database? Can this endpoint be called directly? How much data can one account access before we notice? Where else does this information get replicated? Why do we have this data at all? You think in terms of attack paths, blast radius and least privilege, not just compliance requirements. Pragmatism You know that security engineering is a prioritisation problem. You can distinguish between: something that needs to be fixed this week; something that requires an architectural redesign; something cryptographically elegant but operationally unnecessary. You are comfortable deploying simple, high-impact controls quickly while designing stronger long-term foundations. What would make you stand out Experience with: large-scale SaaS or fintech platforms; highly sensitive or regulated data; multi-tenant architectures; insider risk or data-loss prevention; advanced cryptographic or privacy-enhancing technologies. What success looks like Sensitive data is exposed to fewer systems and people. Access to sensitive resources is increasingly scoped, attributable and auditable. Compromising a single account or service has a limited blast radius. Security controls are increasingly enforced by the platform rather than by process. Product teams can build secure systems faster and with less friction. What this role is not This is not primarily a GRC, SOC, compliance, policy-writing or penetration-testing role. Those disciplines are important, but this role exists to change how our products and systems are engineered. We expect this person to design systems, write code, influence architecture and ship security capabilities into production. Localization of this position This position can be based at our offices in Paris, Toulouse, or Montpellier on a flex-remote basis. Find more English Speaking Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

The acquisition provides us with new expertise, analytics and proprietary technology which is being used to provide risk management and optimisation services to help maximise the value of our clients’ renewable power. integration.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Example Project Areas</strong></p> <p>Depending on the internship opportunity, projects may include working with large trading, market or asset-related datasets, supporting optimisation work linked to renewable assets, PPAs, BESS, balancing risk management or systematic trading strategies, and developing Python-based analytical tools, predictive models, dashboards or workflows.</p> <p><strong>Key Responsibilities</strong></p> <ul> <li>Work closely with a front office team on data-led projects within renewables, power or balancing risk management, trading strategies and, where relevant, automated trading execution.</li> <li>Develop, test or improve analytical tools, models, dashboards or workflows using Python and other relevant tools.</li> decisions.</li> </ul> <p><strong>About You</strong></p> <p>Across our 2027 internship program, we are looking for motivated, intellectually curious individuals who are keen to apply strong analytical and technical skills to real business challenges in power and renewables markets. title: Senior Recruiter (Contractor)
description: About us Founded in 2019 and part of Y Combinator's 2020 cohort, Photoroom is the leading visual solution for e-commerce. We've raised Series B funding and reached 300+ million users worldwide, processing over 5 billion images annually and serving both small businesses and major enterprises like Amazon, DoorDash, and Decathlon through our mobile app, web platform, and API. We're a remote-friendly team of 100+ passionate builders giving e-commerce businesses superpowers to create visuals that help them grow, making the hardest parts of selling online disappear. We focus on craft, innovation, and collaboration, creating exceptional impact for e-commerce businesses worldwide. Role Summary We're looking for a freelance Senior Recruiter to own end-to-end hiring across the business. You'll run searches across the full range of functions we hire for, build pipelines from scratch, and act as a real partner to hiring managers while collaborating closely with the Talent & People team and leaders across GTM, G&A, Product, and Engineering. Our Talent team works full-stack rather than by vertical, so nobody here is boxed into one function, although you may have a primary function to look after during a period of time. Your search list shifts as our hiring priorities do, keeping the work varied and giving you visibility across the whole company. In practice, a single quarter might have you running an Account Executive search, a Finance Manager role, and a Product Designer hire at the same time. Mission: 3-4 month freelance mission running to the end of the year, 4-5 days a week, with the possibility of renewal Location: Paris. The mission involves regular on-site collaboration with hiring managers, and we'd expect you on-site around 3 days a week. Start date: ideally early October, with some flexibility for the right person. About the Role Own the full recruitment cycle, from kickoff and sourcing through to screening and offer. We hold a high bar for candidate experience here: timely, meaningful feedback at every stage, and nobody is left without an answer, no matter where they are in the process. Take on searches across any part of the business, moving between GTM, G&A, Product, and Engineering depending on where our hiring priorities sit. You'd typically be running 5 to 7 live roles at a time. Source actively for most of your roles, as that's where the majority of our pipeline comes from. We care about quality and personalised outreach rather than volume, and you'll balance that with inbound applications and referrals, ensuring your sourcing reaches a genuinely diverse candidate pool. Partner closely with hiring managers to sharpen role scoping, calibrate on what good looks like, and guide them through selection and offer decisions. Balance delivery with improvement. Filling roles comes first, but we expect you to leave our process better than you found it: use pipeline data to spot bottlenecks, and build the tooling and automations that take repetitive work off your plate. We're an AI company, so we encourage AI-native work here rather than something you squeeze in on the side. About You You have 5+ years of recruiting experience, in-house, embedded, or agency-side, with a proven range across very different functions rather than depth in a single vertical. What matters to us is that you've owned searches end-to-end and partnered directly with hiring managers, not just delivered shortlists. You get up to speed quickly on functions you haven't hired for before, using hiring manager conversations, market research, and your own judgment rather than waiting to be taught. You have a strong track record in proactive sourcing and can walk us through hard searches you've filled in the past, including how you built the pipeline. You're an excellent communicator and a proven closer, comfortable holding your own with senior stakeholders across any function. You're hands-on with tools and automation. You can point to something you built, automated, or streamlined that made your hiring work faster or better, whether that's an ATS workflow, a sourcing automation, or an AI-assisted part of your process. We use Ashby, LinkedIn Recruiter, and Claude. You're based in or around Paris, comfortable with regular on-site collaboration, and can start within a short notice period. If you think you have what it takes but don't meet every single point above, please still apply. We'd love to chat and see if you could be a great fit. Mission Details 3-4 month mission , running to the end of the year, 4 to 5 days a week, with the possibility of renewal depending on hiring needs and how the collaboration goes Regular on-site collaboration with hiring managers in our central Paris office, around 3 days a week Access to the tools you need to deliver , including our ATS (Ashby), LinkedIn Recruiter, and AI tools (ex: Claude, Notion AI) Direct access to decision makers , so you can move fast without long approval chains Hiring Process Screening call with Recruiter (30min) Interview with Hiring Manager (30 to 45 min) Short sourcing task (1 hour, sent ahead of the review call) and review call with the team (45min) Culture fit interview (45min) Offer Support: We value diversity and aim to create an inclusive experience for all applicants. Please let us know if there’s anything we can do to make the process more accessible for you. We believe our company and culture are strongest when composed of diverse experiences and backgrounds. That's also why we have flexible working hours, trust people to work remotely, and extended parental leave. All qualified applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to age, color, family, gender identity, marital status, national origin, physical or mental disability, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws. title: Product ML Engineer
description: About us Founded in 2019 and part of Y Combinator's 2020 cohort, Photoroom is the leading visual solution for e-commerce. We've raised Series B funding and reached 300+ million users worldwide, processing over 5 billion images annually and serving both small businesses and major enterprises like Amazon, DoorDash, and Decathlon through our mobile app, web platform, and API. We're a remote-friendly team of 100+ passionate builders giving e-commerce businesses superpowers to create visuals that help them grow, making the hardest parts of selling online disappear. We focus on craft, innovation, and collaboration, creating exceptional impact for e-commerce businesses worldwide. Role Summary We're looking for a Product ML Engineer to join one of our product experience teams — SMB, Scaler or Enterprise — and own the ML side of short, high-impact projects. You'll work on focused ML problems with a clear product outcome, sometimes fine-tuning one of our models, sometimes integrating the best externally available model, but always choosing the fastest and most effective path to customer value. You'll bring the technical depth of an Applied Scientist while operating with the pace and pragmatism of a product engineer. You'll own the journey from framing the problem through to shipping, measuring and iterating on the feature in production. This is not a research role. Your time horizon is weeks rather than quarters, and success is measured by what reaches users and the impact it creates. About the role Embed directly within a product team. Work closely with the SMB, Scaler or Enterprise team on focused ML problems tied to clear customer and business outcomes. Own ML projects end to end. Frame the problem, choose the approach, execute the plan, ship the feature and monitor its performance in production. Make the build vs. buy decision. Determine when to fine-tune or build a model yourself versus integrating an external model, API or existing library. Move from idea to production quickly. Work on projects scoped in weeks rather than quarters, prioritising rapid iteration and customer impact. Work closely with the ML team. Leverage shared infrastructure, evaluation tooling and expertise while remaining embedded in the product team's priorities and cadence. Stay close to users. Get rapid feedback from customers, monitor how people use what you've shipped and use those insights to drive the next iteration. Balance technical depth with pragmatism. Know when deeper modelling work is necessary and when an existing solution is already good enough to ship. Write production code. Work directly in the product team's codebase rather than operating primarily through research notebooks and experiments. Own quality in production. Build sound evaluations, monitor performance and investigate failures once the feature is live. About You You've shipped ML into production. You have 2+ years of hands-on experience building and shipping ML-powered products, with strong experience in PyTorch or equivalent frameworks such as TensorFlow or JAX. You have applied-science depth. You can fine-tune vision or diffusion models, design meaningful evaluations and debug training runs when necessary. You're a pragmatic builder. You care about solving the customer's problem rather than proving that your own model is the best approach. title: Analyst Early Stage Team
description: Analyst Early Stage Investment Team (m/f/d) - Berlin, Munich, London HV Capital is one of Europe's largest generalist VCs. We invest from pre-seed through growth, across SaaS, fintech, deep tech, and beyond. This is a seat inside the investment team, working directly with partners on sourcing, diligence, and portfolio support. What you'll actually work on Finding the next companies before anyone else does. Building market maps in sectors we're excited about, sourcing directly instead of waiting for inbound, running comps, and going deep enough on a space that you know it better than the partner sitting next to you. Running real diligence. Talking to founders, customers, and competitors. Building the model, not just filling in someone else's template. Stress-testing a business case instead of taking the deck at face value. Writing memos that make a case a partner would actually defend in an investment committee. Forming your own view, and holding it. We're still making bets on people as much as products, and that means judgment: reading a founder, reading a room, deciding whether you'd trust this person with your own money. That's a muscle, not a checklist. Sitting in the room, eventually. Partner meetings and deal reviews once you've earned it; not to run them, but to watch how a real investment decision actually gets made, and to have a sharp, well-formed view ready when someone asks for yours. Portfolio support. The odd KPI request, board-prep question, or research ask from a founder who needs a sharp answer fast, not a polished deck in two weeks. What good looks like here We evaluate analysts on judgment and reasoning (can you form an independent view and defend it under pushback), commercial acumen (do you actually understand what makes a business work), deal execution (can you run a process end to end from sourcing, modeling, diligence to closing support), and how you show up in the room. Ownership and curiosity matter as much as any of that. Chasing a thread nobody assigned you, following through without being asked twice. The craft still matters. A clean model, a memo that holds up, a process run properly. That's the baseline, not optional. What increasingly separates a good analyst from a great one on top of that is judgment: forming a view nobody handed you, and holding it under pushback. What we're looking for At least 2 -3 years of real work experience. Beyond that, we don't have one template. About Cloudscaler Cloudscaler is a rapidly growing cloud consultancy. Responsibilities and outcomes Resource matching and assignment Own resource assignments across enterprise and growth client engagements, from incoming demand through to confirmed placement and mobilisation. Match people to work against a rounded set of criteria: skills, experience, career progression goals, team preferences, client need, and personal asks such as location, industry, and preferred way of working. Associate pool sourcing and management Build, curate, and grow a pool of trusted associates who can be called on for flexible or specialist capacity. Own the associate relationship: onboarding, quality assurance, engagement, and offboarding, so associates are ready to deploy and represent Cloudscaler well. Maintain associate records, availability, rates, and compliance status, and match associates to demand on the same criteria used for permanent colleagues. AI and automation Prioritise the use of AI and automation to cut manual effort across resourcing, matching, and reporting. Identify the highest-friction manual tasks and design lighter, tool-supported ways of doing them, in step with the planned automation of the bench report. Help specify and adopt resourcing tooling that gives a single, reliable view of demand, availability, skills, and the associate pool. Champion accurate underlying data. Reporting and stakeholder management Give the Chief Consulting Officer regular, clear management information on availability, assignments, bench position, and associate coverage. Coordinate with the CRO function so resourcing forecast and the sales pipeline stay aligned. Onboarding support for new joiners to ensure a positive first experience of a project (whether internal or client facing) Non-billable bench time held within agreed thresholds, with early flags when the position is moving. A dependable associate pool that can be mobilised at short notice for flexible and specialist needs. Measurable reduction in manual effort across matching and reporting, through AI and automation. Trust from colleagues and managers alike that assignments are fair, transparent, and well matched. Experience Professional background Proven experience in resource management, staffing, workforce planning, or delivery operations, ideally within a consultancy, professional services, or technology environment. A track record of matching people to work against multiple, sometimes competing, criteria. Experience building or managing an associate, contractor, or freelance network is a strong advantage. Comfortable holding the commercial tension between billable utilisation and investment in people. Skills and approach Genuinely AI-first. You reach for automation to remove manual work and can help specify and adopt the right tooling. Highly organised, with strong attention to data accuracy and a calm approach to competing demands. A clear, direct communicator who can set honest expectations and have straightforward conversations about capacity and priorities. Confident working with data and MI, and with systems such as time recording and HR tools. Collaborative and trusted, able to work across delivery, commercial, and People functions. Desirable Familiarity with cloud consultancy delivery and the roles involved, from Project and Engagement Managers through to Cloud Engineers, Consultants, and Architects. Awareness of public sector delivery and security clearance requirements, and how these affect who can be placed on which work. Exposure to IR35 and associated contractor compliance considerations. Experience introducing or improving resourcing tooling and automation. Why Cloudscaler Cloudscaler is scaling rapidly and deliberately. Getting resourcing right is one of the biggest levers we have, and this role owns it. You will have genuine ownership of a new function, the freedom to design how it works, and the mandate to bring AI to bear on work that has always been manual. You will be joining a company that values integrity, community, and mastery, and that backs its people to build things properly. title: Staff Offensive Security Engineer
description: Who we are Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale. Working at Samsara means you'll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that's shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you'll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term. About the role: Samsara sits at the center of hardware, software, AI, and the physical world, processing 25+ trillion data points annually across thousands of connected devices. The Samsara Application Security team protects this vast footprint end-to-end, spanning cloud services, internal systems, and firmware running on IoT hardware in the field. As a Staff Application Security Engineer, you'll drive the overarching technical direction for our application security and vulnerability management programs. This is a high-visibility role where you'll influence a broad surface area while retaining the flexibility to dive deep into critical domain focus areas as security priorities evolve. This is a remote position, open to candidates residing in the UK. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role. You should apply if:  You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely. You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won't be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, and countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper-growth environment. You're energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers. You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-caliber team that will encourage you to do your best. In this role, you will:   Lead the ongoing strategy, operation, and continuous improvement of Samsara's vulnerability management program, along with other core application security programs — not just execute against an existing process, but define what the process should be. Own and drive down mean time to remediate (MTTR) across the vulnerability backlog, as SLAs tighten. Build and champion automation and tooling that scale vulnerability detection and response across cloud, firmware/IoT, and corporate systems, rather than relying on manual, one-by-one review. Set technical and architectural direction for the program, translating leadership's strategic priorities into a concrete execution plan for the team. Drive remediation by building trust with engineering teams and providing clear, actionable guidance — partnering with technical program management on reporting rather than owning it directly. Mentor and level up other engineers on secure design and remediation practices, and be a technical voice other teams look to when priorities are unclear. Communicate risk and remediation tradeoffs to engineering leadership in terms they can act on, without owning the relationship end to end. Participate in security incident investigations involving high-profile vulnerabilities, assessing potential impact on Samsara's infrastructure. Be regularly on call to support critical vulnerability response. Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices Minimum requirements for the role: 10+ years of relevant experience as a cloud engineer or security engineer, including hands-on vulnerability management across a broad, multi-product enterprise environment  — not a single product or team's slice of it. Proficiency in Go, Python, and JavaScript. Demonstrated ability to independently set technical and architectural direction for a security program, and to drive remediation across a broad, multi-surface environment without direct authority over the teams doing the fixing. Significant experience with modern vulnerability management tooling (e.g., Wiz, Semgrep) and deep familiarity with vulnerability scoring frameworks such as CVSS and EPSS. Strong AWS cloud services background. Deep understanding of Static Application Security Testing (SAST), Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST), and Software Composition Analysis (SCA). Hands-on use of AI/LLM tooling in your own security workflow — triage, detection logic, remediation drafting — plus credibility speaking to how AI is changing the threat landscape and the tooling available to address it. description: At Vanta, our mission is to help businesses earn and prove trust. We believe that security should be monitored and verified continuously, and we empower companies to practice better security and prove it with ease. Vanta has a kind and talented team, and while some have prior security experience, many have been successful at Vanta without it. As we continue to expand globally, we’re hiring a Recruiting Coordinator in London to support Vanta’s continued growth and help build scalable, geo-specific recruiting practices in our newest hub. You’ll play a key role in creating an exceptional experience for every candidate, interviewer, and hiring manager in our London and Dublin offices. This is a critical position for someone who thrives in a fast-paced, collaborative environment and is excited about building structure, managing complexity, and driving operational excellence in recruiting. This role is hybrid in person in our London office. What you’ll do as a Recruiting Coordinator at Vanta: Coordinate interviews across teams, time zones, and formats (virtual and in-person), ensuring a smooth candidate experience Own candidate communications, including scheduling emails and interview prep materials Manage onsite interview logistics in the London office, including day-of setup and support Help plan and execute in-person recruiting events in partnership with the Talent and Workplace teams Build and document EMEA specific recruiting processes and candidate communications Set up jobs and interview plans in Ashby, and keep all scheduling data accurate and up to date Partner with recruiters and hiring managers to update interview processes and flag workflow issues Support interviewer training by tracking completion and sharing resources with new interviewers Monitor compliance tasks, including NDA tracking and weekly Checkr background check audits How to be successful in this role: 2+ years of experience as a Recruiting Coordinator or similar role in a fast-paced, high-growth tech environment, ideally supporting distributed teams or international hiring Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage competing priorities A proactive mindset to spot inefficiencies, propose solutions, and follow through to make them happen A true team player with a service-oriented approach and an eye for providing a warm, seamless experience for candidates and interviewers Excitement to be a foundational hire in London, helping shape our on-the-ground recruiting practices and office culture Open to using AI to amplify their skills and strengthen their work - demonstrating curiosity, a willingness to learn, and sound judgment in applying AI responsibly to improve efficiency and impact. What you can expect as a Vanta’n in the UK: Industry-competitive salary and equity 100% covered medical, dental, and vision benefits with dependents coverage 16 weeks paid Parental Leave for all new parents Health & wellness stipend Remote workspace, internet, and mobile phone stipend Commuter benefits for team members who attend the office Pension matching 25 days of Annual Leave per year and unlimited sick time 8 company-paid holidays Virtual team building activities, lunch and learns, and other company-wide events! Offices in SF, NYC, London, Dublin, Tel Aviv, and Sydney #LI-hybrid At Vanta, we are committed to hiring diverse talent of different backgrounds and as such, it is important to us to provide an inclusive work environment for all. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, gender identity, age, religion, sexual orientation, veteran or disability status, or any other protected class. As an equal opportunity employer, we encourage and welcome people of all backgrounds to apply. About Vanta We started in 2018, in the wake of several high-profile data breaches. Online security was only becoming more important, but we knew firsthand how hard it could be for fast-growing companies to invest the time and manpower it takes to build a solid security foundation. Vanta was inspired by a vision to restore trust in internet businesses by enabling companies to improve and prove their security. Now more than ever, making security continuous—not just a point-in-time check— is essential. Thousands of companies rely on Vanta to build, maintain and demonstrate their trust— all in a way that's real-time and transparent. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future. Your primary focus is hunting new business opportunities, building sales pipeline, and driving growth within the SMB sector. You are also responsible for upselling into the existing account base, leveraging our Extended Access Management platform. You will own a specific geographical region or country within the EMEA market. How we’re using AI today Across GTM, we’re transforming the way we work with AI. We expect every seller, CSM, and team member to become a power user, using it daily to work smarter and move faster. AI is already embedded in how we operate – from real-time coaching that sharpens how we sell and interact with customers, to surfacing insights that help us anticipate needs – creating more time for meaningful customer engagement. Manage Pipeline: Build and maintain a healthy sales pipeline through proactive prospecting, inbound leads, cold calling, and networking, utilizing our formalized sales process, MEDDPPICC. title: Senior Software Engineer (Ruby), Security Platform: Authorization
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values&nbsp;and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h4><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h4> <p>As a Senior Software Engineer on GitLab's Authorization team, you will own significant parts of the system that decides what every user, token, and automated agent can access on GitLab.com, Self-Managed, and Dedicated.</p> <p>Today that work is Ruby on Rails. Roughly 400 policy classes and a YAML catalog of about 1,900 permissions sit behind every API request. You will work on the permission model itself (fine-grained token permissions, custom roles, and the GraphQL and REST surfaces that enforce them). You will also help move that model onto GitLab's next-generation authorization stack, which pairs the Rails monolith with a Rust policy engine using Zanzibar-style relationship tuples and Cedar policies. The monolith already loads that engine in-process and can reach it over gRPC.</p> <p>Some examples of our projects:</p> <ul> <li>Refactoring GitLab's policy layer so the same permission definitions can be evaluated by the monolith and by our new authorization service</li> <li>Extending fine-grained token permissions to more resources and more kinds of principal, including the service identities behind AI agents</li> <li>Bringing GitLab's first modular service, Artifact Registry, onto the new authorization stack</li> <li>Isolating custom-role and permission data per organization ahead of GitLab Cells</li> </ul> <h4><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h4> <ul> <li>Design and ship authorization changes in GitLab's Ruby on Rails monolith, where a single request can trigger hundreds of permission checks.</li> <li>Own a workstream end to end. Problem definition through feature-flagged rollout, dual-run verification, and cleanup.</li> <li>Build and extend fine-grained permissions for tokens and roles, and keep the permission catalog coherent as it grows.</li> <li>Extend and harden authorization enforcement across GraphQL and the REST API.</li> <li>Refactor long-lived policy code so both the monolith and our new authorization engine can evaluate it, without changing behavior for existing customers.</li> <li>Improve the reliability, performance, and security posture of existing authorization systems, including paying down permission-model debt.</li> <li>Partner with the authentication, platform, AI, and modular-service teams on interface contracts as authorization moves toward a shared service.</li> <li>Drive technical decisions in writing. Design docs, architecture decision records, and code review, in a fully asynchronous organization.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h4> <ul> <li>Significant experience building and operating production Ruby on Rails applications.</li> <li>Experience designing or implementing authorization systems, including role-based access control and fine-grained permissions.</li> <li>A security mindset. You treat a permission bug as a security bug, and you reason about blast radius before elegance.</li> <li>Comfort making careful changes to large, long-lived codebases. Incremental refactors, feature-flagged rollouts, and migrations that must not change behavior for existing users.</li> <li>Working knowledge of GraphQL and API authorization patterns.</li> <li>Attention to performance at scale. You understand why one uncached check matters when it runs hundreds of times per request.</li> <li>Strong written communication. You are effective when most decisions happen in a document or a merge request rather than a meeting.</li> <li>Helpful but not required: Rust, gRPC or Protocol Buffers, Cedar or other policy languages, Zanzibar-style authorization systems, Go, or service-oriented architecture. Several engineers on this team picked up Rust for this work and we will support you doing the same.</li> <li>We welcome transferable experience from adjacent domains such as identity, policy engines, and platform security.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>About the team</strong></h4> <p>The Authorization team owns the capabilities that determine what users, tokens, and automated agents can access across GitLab. Our work runs on two tracks. We are strengthening the permission model inside the Ruby on Rails monolith (fine-grained token permissions, custom roles, and the policy layer that enforces them), and we are moving that model onto a shared authorization platform built for GitLab's modular and cell-based future.</p> <p>We work closely with the teams building GitLab's authentication layer, its Rust authorization engine, and the first modular services adopting it. description: <p><strong>Data Scientist | Logistics &amp; Fulfilment | Hybrid Working | London</strong></p> <p><strong>Introduction:</strong>&nbsp;</p> <p>We are Ocado Group, and we're bringing world-class automation to online grocery. Our Ocado Smart Platform (OSP) combines cutting-edge robotics, AI, and IoT within our advanced CFCs (Customer Fulfilment Centres). We've mastered the single pick, transforming online delivery for our global partners. Join us and be part of a team pushing the boundaries of retail technology.</p> <p><strong>About the Role</strong>&nbsp;</p> <p>As a Data Scientist in our Treefrogs team, you will play a key role in powering the machine learning algorithms behind Ocado Group’s Logistics and Supply Chain technology. Our mission-critical models drive key operational decisions for global partners, including demand forecasting, drive-time predictions, and supplier reliability. In this role, you will own the full data science lifecycle, from researching state-of-the-art deep learning techniques to deploying, scaling, and supporting production-ready models.</p> <p>Working closely with cross-functional software engineering, data engineering, and product teams, you will tackle high-impact problems where algorithm performance directly affects operational efficiency and partner revenue. You will continuously refine existing architectures, build robust data pipelines, and explore new applications for machine learning, ensuring our systems remain reliable, scalable, and cutting-edge.</p> <p><strong>Key Responsibilities</strong></p> <ul> <li>Improve existing model architectures and adapt them to solve new operational challenges and support global partner expansions.</li> <li>Design and build scalable data pipelines to feed richer, high-quality data into machine learning models.</li> <li>Own, support, and maintain machine learning models in production environments, ensuring high availability and performance.</li> <li>Collaborate with Product teams to identify, define, and build new machine learning applications across our stream.</li> <li>Work alongside Software Engineering teams to design robust interfaces between machine learning models and broader software systems.</li> <li>Communicate complex technical findings and model performance clearly to both internal and external stakeholders.</li> <li>Promote and uphold best practices in machine learning development, testing, and continuous deployment.</li> <li>Stay up to date with the latest machine learning research to identify and implement innovative techniques.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What We’re Looking For</strong></p> <p><em>Essential</em></p> <ul> <li>Strong programming proficiency in Python and solid knowledge of SQL.</li> <li>Practical experience working with Google Cloud Platform (GCP).</li> <li>Either 2+ years of data science experience with an emphasis on productionising models, OR 2+ years in a software/data engineering role with formal study in machine learning.</li> <li>Good comprehension of fundamental machine learning concepts.</li> <li>Familiarity with modern software development processes, including code reviews, CI/CD, testing, and documentation.</li> <li>Ability to document and explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences.</li> </ul> <p><em>Nice to Haves</em></p> <ul> <li>Experience with deep learning frameworks such as TensorFlow or Keras.</li> <li>Knowledge of time-series modelling techniques, particularly transformers.</li> <li>Experience working with geospatial data and geospatial modelling techniques.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Benefits</strong>&nbsp;</p> <p>We believe in supporting our people with meaningful, flexible benefits that prioritise well-being and work-life balance. Here’s a snapshot of what you can expect:</p> <ul> <li>Time to recharge: 25 days annual leave (rising to 27 after 5 years), plus the option to buy more – and 30 days a year to work from anywhere in the world.</li> <li>Health &amp; wellbeing: Private Medical Insurance from your first month, wellbeing support through specialist apps and EAP, plus Income Protection and Life Assurance.</li> <li>Family-first policies: 22 weeks paid maternity/primary carer leave and 6 weeks paid paternity leave</li> <li>Financial support: Pension with employer matching up to 7%, share schemes (Sharesave &amp; BAYE), and interest-free loans for train tickets.</li> <li>Commuter perks: Cycle to Work Scheme and free shuttle buses to/from Hatfield and Welwyn Garden City stations.</li> <li>Exclusive discounts: 15% off at Ocado.com with free delivery (starting in your first month).</li> </ul> <p>Be bold, be unique, be brilliant, be you. We are committed to making reasonable adjustments to provide a positive, barrier-free recruitment process and supportive work environment. Our platform gives businesses of all sizes, from independent jewellers to major retail chains access to the world's best diamond and gemstone inventory, without the traditional barriers of capital, geography, or information asymmetry. Nivoda was built to change that - to democratise access and empower every business, regardless of size or location, to buy and sell with confidence. Independent jewellers are at the heart of this mission. They deserve the same access to quality, pricing, and selection as the biggest players in the industry. That's exactly what we give them. This is a team that thrives on commercial creativity, deep customer relationships, and relentless execution and we're growing fast. A killer on the phone and crisp in writing; comfortable with 60–80+ meaningful touches a day. Process-driven: you live in cadences and CRM hygiene rather than fighting them. Coachable and resilient — you treat "no" as data and keep the energy up on day 20 of the month, not just day 1. Native or professional proficiency in English, Dutch, Flemish & French is required for this role. Jewellery knowledge not required; hunger and rigour are. Our culture and what we offer 😉 At Nivoda, we believe that employees today want to evolve in a collaborative, high-growth environment where they can demonstrate their abilities and thrive both professionally and personally. We work to create a culture of empowerment, continuous learning, and growth where everyone can bring their expertise, own projects, and easily measure their impact. Dynamic working environment in a rapidly growing company. Enjoy a pleasant, low-hierarchy work environment. Engage in intellectually challenging work that contributes significantly to Nivoda's success and scalability. We don't discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status or disability status. Strengthen CI/CD practices in GitHub Actions, establishing repeatable deployment patterns, environment promotions, automated rollbacks, and release controls . Enablement & Integration Deploy vector database and retrieval infrastructure (e.g., Databricks AI Search) to support Document AI and RAG use cases . Diagnose and resolve charger malfunctions, communication issues, and electrical, electronic, or control-system faults. MSF International Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation. MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s 24 sections, 28 associations and 19 branch offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested. II. CONTEXT One of the objectives of the pharma network is to assure the quality of medicines in MSF projects. The pharma network is mainly composed of pharmacists working in the medical departments of the operational centers (section pharmacists, pharmacy advisors), pharmacists in European Supply Centres (ESC), pharmacists in the Access Campaign / Access to Products for Healthcare and regional/intersectional pharmacists. Coordination of this network is done by the International Pharmacist Coordinator (IPC) who has a permanent position within the International Office. Main activities of the International Pharmaceutical Coordination team (from an International QA perspective) are: To maintain the coherence of the MSF pharma network, where the Drugs QA Leader focuses on the quality related ESC groups composed not only of pharmacists, but also ESC buyers. To coordinate the implementation of the MSF Qualification Scheme for international procurement and all related activities with the support of external experts, when needed. This is a key responsibility of the Drugs QA Leader. To facilitate and ensure that common specifications and procedures are implemented and used in all sections and ESCs – the Drugs QA Leader focuses on the coordination within the ESCs. To participate to external networks/meetings with other key international actors (UNICEF, WHO, ICRC…) sharing the objectives to improve quality of medicines on the international market. The Drugs QA Leader builds and maintains external collaborations linked to quality related topics. III. PURPOSE OF THE JOB Lead the MSF Drug Quality Assurance activities in order to identify new quality sources of drug supply, consolidate the MSF drug QA system to ensure quality, safe and efficacious medicines are used by MSF patients and achieve a coordinated approach towards quality medicines within the ESCs to increase synergies and gains efficiency, as well as monitor international regulatory developments and dynamics that may have an impact on MSF. IV. KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES The extent to which a job is answerable for actions and their consequences. It describes the area and nature of impact of the job on the organisation. Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies in terms of identifying, selecting and adding to MSF database repository: Coordinates and leads the ESCs (QAs and buyers) in all pharmaceutical aspects linked to the search of sources, selection and use of essential medicines identified as priority. Coordinates with SPINCO and working groups for any inclusion or changes to MSF catalogues and coordinates the QA/supply check related to new medicines requests. Identifies strategic opportunities and risks to manage and continue to develop the MSF Quality Management System (QMS): Responsible for the creation and revision of the MSF Quality Management System for medicines. Ensures proper updating and storage and communicates changes to the relevant pharmacists (IMES, IPC, pharma network). title: Director of Product Marketing and Market Research
description: <div class="content-intro"><h4><strong>Help make the world more hospitable </strong></h4> <p>The hospitality industry is uniquely human, and it deserves technology that’s just as inspiring as the people behind it. At Mews, we’re transforming the industry with a platform that helps hotels run smarter, move faster and create better guest experiences.</p> <p>You’ll work with smart, curious people who care deeply about what they do. You’ll have autonomy and the trust to make good decisions and move quickly. And you’ll enjoy a real sense of purpose as you see the impact of what we’re building.</p> <p>If you’re motivated by ownership, curiosity and meaningful impact, and are driven to deliver consistent high performance, you’ll feel at home here.</p> <h4><strong>About the role</strong></h4> <p>Let's get into the specifics. It’s impossible to capture every nuance of a role – especially at a rapidly growing company like Mews – but if we had to distil it into a job description (which we do because this is a job description), it would be this:</p></div><h3>POSITION OVERVIEW</h3> <p>Product marketing at Mews is at a turning point. The function has been effective at launching products; what it has not yet built is the strategic layer that comes after launch – the continuous positioning, adoption strategy, and market intelligence that makes each product more valuable over time. This role owns that shift.</p> <p>The Director of Product Marketing and Market Research is a combined senior leadership role responsible for two things that should never have been separated: how Mews brings products to market, and how Mews understands the market it operates in. You will lead the product marketing team, own the research and customer insights function, and serve as the go-to authority on both disciplines for senior leadership across the business.</p> <p>Mews operates across property management, fintech and payments, guest experience, and marketplace. The right person for this role knows how to build a coherent positioning story across a complex multi-product portfolio – and how to ground that story in real market intelligence, customer insight, and competitive understanding rather than assumption.</p> <h3>RESPONSIBILITIES</h3> <h3>Product marketing strategy</h3> <ul> <li> <p>Define and own product marketing strategy across the Mews portfolio – covering positioning, messaging, and go-to-market execution from launch through adoption and ongoing engagement.</p> </li> <li> <p>Build and govern the global product launch framework so that launches are scalable and repeatable, with clear handoffs between strategy and execution.</p> </li> <li> <p>Own product adoption and post-launch engagement strategy – moving the function beyond launch execution to continuous market thinking that drives usage, retention, and revenue contribution.</p> </li> <li> <p>Partner with Product, Sales, RevOps, and Customer Success to ensure product marketing strategy connects to commercial outcomes and is reflected in how the business goes to market.</p> </li> <li> <p>Own NPS tracking programs and design the measurement framework for product marketing impact, including product attach rates, adoption metrics, and pipeline contribution.</p> </li> </ul> <h3>Market research and customer insights</h3> <ul> <li> <p>Own the end-to-end market research function: identifying research opportunities, designing methodology, running studies, synthesising findings, and activating insights across the business.</p> </li> <li> <p>Lead primary and secondary research initiatives that inform strategic, commercial, and product decisions – including competitive analysis, customer behaviour, market sizing, and buyer intelligence.</p> </li> <li> <p>Build competitive intelligence as a structured, ongoing discipline – not a one-off project. Translate competitive signals into positioning decisions, sales enablement, and product roadmap input.</p> </li> <li> <p>Serve as the functional authority on what the market is telling Mews, and translate that into insight narratives that influence senior leadership decisions and business strategy.</p> </li> <li> <p>Work closely with Strategy, Product, RevOps, and Marketing to ensure insights land where decisions get made, not just where they get read.</p> </li> </ul> <h3>Team and function leadership</h3> <ul> <li> <p>Lead and develop a team of product marketers, setting clear expectations, building capability, and creating a culture of commercial accountability.</p> </li> <li> <p>Set the operating model for how the team works with AI – determining where AI handles execution tasks and where human judgment is irreplaceable, and building team-level standards accordingly.</p> </li> <li> <p>Serve as the senior leadership go-to on product marketing and market intelligence – the person any executive can trust for a well-grounded, commercially-connected answer.</p> </li> <li> <p>Represent product marketing and research in executive forums, contributing to annual planning and portfolio prioritisation decisions.</p> </li> </ul> <h3>REQUIREMENTS</h3> <h3>Professional knowledge and experience</h3> <ul> <li> <p>10+ years in B2B SaaS marketing, with the majority of that time in product marketing – not demand generation, not agency, not brand-only roles.</p> </li> <li> <p>Has held a Director, Senior Director, or Head of Product Marketing title, or a broader marketing leadership title that included ownership of the product marketing function.</p> </li> <li> <p>Proven track record managing and developing a multi-person product marketing team, including hiring, coaching, and performance management.</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience owning or significantly contributing to a market research or customer insights function – primary research methodology, competitive intelligence programs, or voice-of-customer work.</p> </li> <li> <p>Deep understanding of B2B SaaS go-to-market strategy: positioning, messaging architecture, pricing and packaging alignment, sales enablement, and lifecycle marketing.</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience building or significantly reshaping a product marketing function – not just managing an inherited one.</p> </li> <li> <p>Has operated in a lean, fast-moving environment such as a scale-up, growth-stage, or pre-IPO company. Experience only in large enterprise environments with unlimited resources is unlikely to be a strong fit.</p> </li> </ul> <h3>Skills and capabilities</h3> <ul> <li> <p>Owns GTM strategy end-to-end – from initial positioning through post-launch adoption and continuous market engagement. Experience limited to launch execution is not sufficient.</p> </li> <li> <p>Connects product marketing directly to revenue outcomes. Can articulate how their work has influenced pipeline, product attach rates, adoption, or retention – not just campaign outputs.</p> </li> <li> <p>Translates research into business decisions – not just insight reports. Has a track record of research that changed a strategic or commercial direction.</p> </li> <li> <p>Multi-functional marketing experience beyond product marketing, for example content, SEO, digital, demand generation, or go-to-market strategy.</p> </li> <li> <p>Metrics-driven. Comfortable defining and owning the measurement framework for both product marketing impact and research quality.</p> </li> <li> <p>Strong senior stakeholder communication. Able to influence executive decisions, present with authority, and earn trust through substance rather than seniority alone.</p> </li> <li> <p>Publicly visible in the product marketing or insights community – speaker, writer, or recognised contributor to the discipline. Not a requirement, but a meaningful differentiator.</p> </li> </ul> <h3>AI fluency</h3> <p>AI is changing the product marketing function in a way that is more structural than any other recent technology shift. A significant part of this role is deciding what that means for the team at Mews – what AI handles, what stays human, and how to build a team that operates at a higher strategic level as execution work is automated.</p> <p>We expect this person to: use AI tools deliberately and with criteria; describe specific examples of AI changing how they or their team works strategically; have a point of view on where the product marketing function is heading as AI matures; and build team-level standards for AI use, including how to review and quality-control AI-assisted outputs before they reach senior stakeholders or customers.</p> <h3>NICE TO HAVE</h3> <ul> <li> <p>Fintech, payments, or financial services product marketing experience.</p> </li> <li> <p>Hospitality, travel tech, or hotel SaaS background.</p> </li> <li> <p>Both fintech and hospitality in one profile is the strongest possible combination for this role.</p> </li> <li> <p>Global market experience.</p> </li> <li> title: Lead AI Engineer, Agentic Systems - Capco AI Lab
description: <p>We're looking for a Lead AI Engineer to join Capco's AI Frontier Lab, based in Paris.</p> <p>The Lab builds agentic AI solutions for clients in financial services and energy, and advises them on AI architecture and governance. The engineering team is already in place. What's missing is a senior technical lead who owns the architecture, reviews and shapes the team's work, still writes code, and can represent those technical decisions directly to the client.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>What you'll do</strong></p> <p><strong>Lead the engineering (~40%)</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own the architecture of our agentic solutions end to end: orchestration, tool and function calling, memory and state, retrieval, evaluation, observability, plus the cost and latency budgets that decide whether a system survives contact with production.</li> <li>Guide our engineers through design reviews, pairing and code review, raising the bar rather than quietly doing the work for them.</li> <li>Set the standards: reference architectures, agentic patterns, guardrails, testing and eval strategy, CI/CD for non-deterministic systems, deployment topology.</li> <li>Make the build/buy/adapt calls on frameworks, models and platforms, and be able to defend them a year later.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Stay hands-on (~30%)</strong></p> <ul> <li>Prototype fast, and build the hard parts yourself: the tricky orchestration, the eval harness, the integration nobody else wants to touch.</li> <li>Take promising prototypes to production grade, covering reliability, monitoring, versioning, rollback and human-in-the-loop where it matters.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Work with clients (~30%)</strong></p> <ul> <li>Act as our senior technical voice in solution discussions, workshops and pitches, translating between business outcomes and system design in both directions.</li> <li>Advise on AI architecture, platform strategy, model and vendor strategy, and governance as they actually apply to a client's operating model.</li> <li>Produce content that carries weight: reference architectures, points of view, whitepapers, and talks at client forums and conferences.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What we're looking for</strong></p> <p><strong>Essential</strong></p> <ul> <li>8+ years in software or data engineering, including genuine enterprise architecture experience. You've designed systems that had to survive security review, integration hell and real production traffic.</li> <li>You still write code, and you'd be comfortable opening a pull request in your second week. Strong Python or equivalent.</li> <li>Demonstrable agentic AI experience: agentic loops and orchestration, tool use and function calling, multi-agent patterns, MCP or comparable integration approaches, and, critically, how you evaluate AI solutions.</li> <li>Depth on at least one major cloud platform, with the surrounding discipline: containers, IaC, observability, security.</li> <li>Presence with clients. You can hold a room of senior stakeholders, disagree respectfully, and explain a trade-off without retreating into jargon.</li> <li>A real interest in making other engineers better. This role is measured partly by what the team can do without you.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Valuable additions</strong></p> <ul> <li>Domain experience in financial services or energy, and an understanding of what regulation means for system design in those sectors.</li> <li>A consulting or client-facing delivery background.</li> <li>Open-source contributions, publications, or a speaking track record.</li> <li>Hands-on AI governance, risk or assurance work.</li> <li>French alongside fluent English.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What we offer</strong></p> <ul> <li>A Lab with a real mandate and real clients. The work ships, and you'll see it running.</li> <li>Influence over technical direction from day one, not after a two-year wait.</li> <li>The rare combination of deep engineering and senior advisory work, without having to give up either.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> Find more English Speaking Jobs in France on Arbeitnow
